findings.evidence: features/006-insights-skill/006-insights-skill-prd.md:R3 + Schema Appendix — R3 says 'v1 does NOT ship embedding-based clustering. The report schema reserves a `semantic` cluster-source label (alongside `field-shape` and `token-ngram`) so a v2 embedding pass can land additively without breaking the v1 report shape.' The Schema Appendix's cluster-object shape includes `cluster_source: "field-shape" | "token-ngram" | "semantic" # semantic reserved for v2` and the runs.jsonl shape ships a `semantic_clusters: 0` counter. AC-3 enforces the v1 ban: 'A v1 run that emits a cluster with `cluster_source: "semantic"` is a failed run.' The interview's Round 1 resolution names embedding-based clustering as v2-deferred; no v2 PRD exists yet; no documented consumer has asked for the semantic source. Reserving the schema slot for an unrequested v2 capability is the textbook shape of speculative configurability — the v1 schema carries a v2 hook before any v2 user has surfaced.
findings.claim: Speculative configurability — R3 + Schema Appendix reserve a `semantic` cluster-source label and a `semantic_clusters` runs.jsonl counter for a v2 capability that no documented consumer has asked for. CORE_PRINCIPLES.md Simplicity First sub-clause: 'Do not introduce config knobs without a concrete second consumer demanding them. Do not generalise on the first instance. Wait for the second.' The semantic-label reservation generalises on the first instance (v1's two cluster sources). Adding the third source later when a real consumer surfaces is a single schema-revision PR; reserving the slot now adds surface area for zero current value.
findings.proposed_change: Drop the `semantic` cluster-source label and the `semantic_clusters` runs.jsonl counter from the v1 Schema Appendix. The cluster-object shape becomes `cluster_source: "field-shape" | "token-ngram"`; the runs.jsonl shape drops the `semantic_clusters: 0` line. AC-3 simplifies to: 'Every cluster object emitted by v1 has `cluster_source ∈ {"field-shape", "token-ngram"}`; no other source is permitted.' R3 retains the v2-deferral language but drops the schema-reservation clause. When v2 ships embedding-based clustering, the schema gets a coordinated revision (one-line additions to the cluster-object enum + runs.jsonl counter); the cost of that revision is single-digit minutes against the cost of carrying a never-fires schema slot for the entire v1 lifetime.
